criteria.rationale: I checked L1 and L2 against the spec and D1/D2 against the parser, plan and bundle code. L2 is verified by digest binding and the empty-limit compatibility test. L1 leaves semantic breadth to the reviewer; the lexical weakness in N1 is disclosed as an accepted L1 follow-up.
The change adds deterministic parsing and synchronous ADR reads, with no shared mutable state, goroutines, cancellation hooks or background lifecycle.
The review plan, bundle and finding additions are optional JSON fields; the brief moved to /11 and prior templates remain versioned. Tests cover the new conclusion contract.
The new ADR input path is unbounded and follows symlinks, allowing repository input to hang or exhaust the linter.
No HTTP, event or external MCP contract was changed. The integration assessment's three unobserved HTTP consumers are unrelated endpoints; the scoped review path has sealed integration coverage.
A non-terminating or very large ADR target can prevent any bounded diagnostic from being returned.
I checked additive fields use omitempty, the plan and bundle digest tests preserve the no-limit form, and review-brief/11 preserves earlier immutable template versions.
The ready-check's word-count heuristic admits a placeholder-only assumption and reason; this is accepted only as the L1 reviewer-judgment follow-up.

The spec identifies non-converging rounds caused by unstated environmental assumptions. D1 makes limit classification an explicit reviewer judgment; D2 seals the same limits into plan and bundle digests. The structural assessment reported no deltas to map.
I compared POSE.md, the Portuguese manual, and both scaffold copies with runtime parsing, review-brief/11, and within-limit recording; the documented flow matches those behaviors.
Ordinary unreadable ADRs produce actionable errors, but a symlink to an unbounded source can hang the ready-check without a returned diagnostic.
R1-R3 are supported by the parsed/sealed brief and conclusion paths; R4's format gate accepts the placeholder-only text described in N1, an L1 follow-up.
I compared the attributed subject with the spec's plan: parser, CLI ready-check, plan/bundle/conclusion/brief code, tests, manuals and scaffold copies all serve the declared capability.
The ready-check follows repository-controlled ADR symlinks and reads without a bound, crossing the project path boundary and enabling resource exhaustion.

I compared lint-only handling with the selected plan/bundle/brief/conclusion flow: sealing is needed so later review uses the reviewed limits, while omitted fields preserve old records. No general threat-model DSL was added. Revisit this choice if policy requires machine-verifiable semantic matching between finding text and limit text.

findings.rationale: The lexical gate accepts placeholder-like text such as “X. Y. Accepted because z w.” because it counts letter runs, not substantive assumptions or reasons. This is a format-only residual within L1: the sealed brief exposes the limit text for the reviewer to judge and dispute.

findings.action: The ready-check reads each ADR Markdown path with unbounded os.ReadFile and follows symlinks. A repository-controlled ADR symlink can escape the project root or target a non-terminating/huge source such as /dev/zero, hanging the check or exhausting memory.
